title: RES: A Robust Framework for Guiding Visual Explanation

problem.claim: Explanation quality, including explanation accuracy and ways to improve inaccurate explanations, remains under-explored for modern DNN explanation techniques.

gap.claim: Supervising visual explanations through saliency maps faces inaccurate boundaries, incomplete regions, and inconsistent distributions between human annotations and model explanation maps.

contributions.claim: A generic RES framework guides visual explanations by addressing inaccurate boundaries, incomplete regions, and inconsistent distributions in human annotations.
The framework includes a theoretical justification concerning model generalizability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly propose a novel objective for handling inaccurate boundaries, incomplete regions, and inconsistent annotation distributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world image datasets demonstrate improved explanation reasonability and backbone DNN performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Explanation quality and methods for correcting inaccurate explanations are relatively under-explored.
Explanation supervision has shown promising effects on DNN generalizability and intrinsic interpretability.
Visual explanation supervision is at an early stage because of annotation boundary, region completeness, and distribution consistency challenges.
The RES framework introduces an objective for robust visual explanation guidance and provides theoretical justification related to generalizability.
Experiments on two real-world image datasets report gains in explanation reasonability and backbone DNN performance.

source_observation.claim: Human explanation annotations may have inaccurate boundaries, incomplete regions, and distributions inconsistent with model explanation maps.

interpretation.claim: Explanation supervision should account for annotation imperfections and distribution mismatch rather than treating human annotations as exact targets.

application.claim: When designing visual explanation guidance, explicitly model boundary uncertainty, missing relevant regions, and annotation-to-model distribution differences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach applies beyond vision-based saliency-map settings.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework is reported to improve both explanation reasonability and backbone DNN performance on two real-world image datasets.

interpretation.claim: Explanation supervision may affect both interpretability-related outcomes and predictive model performance.

application.claim: Evaluate explanation-guidance methods using both explanation-quality measures and backbone-model performance measures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the RES objective formulation or optimization procedure.
The abstract does not identify the two datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical justification or its assumptions.
